solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scottish island to have a go at crime

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An islander in Scotland decides to attempt a spot of lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: BARRA is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides. The answer is an old offence: fraud or gross negligence by a ship's master against the owners.
explanation.definitionFit: Barratry is a legal term for a maritime offence, so it is a kind of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Order fellows into risky venture

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the fellows go in the bet

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky venture
hes are males, fellows

explanation.surface: Instructing some men to join a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellows' gives HES, plural of he as a noun for a male.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in 'at his behest'.

clue.text: Rod turns up with Heather, whooping it up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lever is a rod used to prise
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Rod arrives with Heather, and they party hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod and Heather look like names but are a lever and a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To be revelling is to celebrate noisily, partying hard.

clue.text: Mound is a new work: last of earth going in

indicators.note: going in means placed inside the work word

parts.note: to till soil is to work it

indicators.note: last of means the final letter

explanation.surface: A heap of earth is a fresh creation, the final soil being added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthill is a heap of earth piled up by ants building their nest.

clue.text: One telling tale about naughty woman

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve disobeyed in Eden by eating the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: A gossip spreading stories about a wicked woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reeve is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims and tells The Reeve's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales the steward pilgrim tells a story, so he is a teller of a tale.

clue.text: Time to encounter sorceress in the grass

parts.note: a sorceress is a witch

explanation.surface: A moment of meeting a witch out in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to encounter' is only a link joining the two pieces. The grass here is couch grass, a weed also called twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitch is another name for couch grass, a creeping weed of lawns and gardens.

clue.text: Ground wanted around lake? Don't build on it, surely?

indicators.note: around means the anagram surrounds the lake letter
ground as a past participle means milled into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Land is wanted by developers, but a lake means building here is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as a noun but signals the anagram of WANTED, which goes around L. The whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy, waterlogged land is unsuited to building, so it is somewhere not to build.

clue.text: Quarrels difficult to deal with, leader being put down

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting the leading letter down moves it to the bottom

parts.note: stiff means hard or tough, as in a stiff test

explanation.surface: Tricky disputes where a boss is humbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader being put down' moves the S of STIFF to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffs are petty squabbles or minor disagreements.

clue.text: Get on well, having success with one swell guy

parts.note: a hit is a success
I is the Roman numeral one
a toff is a smart, upper-class man, a swell

explanation.surface: Getting along nicely by scoring with a fashionable man.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh, well-dressed man.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to form an instant good relationship with someone.

clue.text: Cattle going to water in Scotland, being smart

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle
Loch Ness is a famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Cows heading to a Highland loch, looking spruce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' is a link. NEAT for cattle is an old term, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smart in appearance means tidiness and good order.

clue.text: Possess top-class modern technology to gain advantage

definitions.meaning: a jokey reading: own the finest IT, information technology
to come out on top in a contest or exchange

explanation.surface: Owning the finest gadgets gives you the edge over rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is playful: 'it' is taken as IT, information technology, so possessing the best of it means owning top-class tech.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to come off better or win the upper hand in a situation.

clue.text: Cross gentleman nabbing a commissioned officer

indicators.note: nabbing means seizing, so the gentleman word holds the other pieces

parts.note: sire is an old respectful address to a gentleman or lord
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a commissioned officer

explanation.surface: An angry gentleman grabs an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is a noun: the diagonal cross of St Andrew on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a heraldic X-shaped diagonal cross, as on Scotland's flag.

clue.text: Passage of time managed by model

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A model ran the show for a while as time passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link putting the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage or conveyance from one place to another.

clue.text: Water flowing badly, river choked by spicy stuff

indicators.note: choked by means stuffed inside, so the spice word surrounds the others

parts.note: mace is a spice made from nutmeg husks
ill as an adverb means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A stream that runs poorly because a river is clogged with spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water flowing badly' looks like one phrase, but 'badly' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of fast-moving water that drives a mill wheel.

clue.text: African party on estate with men, one from a previous generation

parts.note: the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress
EST is the abbreviation for estate
OR, Other Ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, men

explanation.surface: A political party gathered on a country estate with some workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from an earlier generation of the family.

clue.text: Coffee encountered, getting knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over suggests something upended, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to have faced something is to have encountered it

explanation.surface: Someone met with a cup of coffee and spilled it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting knocked over' turns FACED round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is the everyday short name for decaffeinated coffee.

clue.text: Sir dealt with cheats, fearsome disciplinarian?

indicators.note: dealt with suggests handled roughly or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A knight punished some cheats like a stern schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' rearranges SIR with CHEATS; the surface also suggests the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who punishes or rebukes severely is a stern enforcer of discipline.

clue.text: Like rock when submerged by sea

indicators.note: submerged by means put inside the sea word

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Rocks seen as they go under the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' gives AS; the definition is an adjective phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Basaltic means made of basalt, a dark volcanic rock.

clue.text: Retro record by the French star

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
la is the French feminine form of the

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned disc made by a French celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' reverses both LOG and LA together, giving ALGOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Algol is a famous variable star in the constellation Perseus.

clue.text: Animated demon about to capture loveless one

indicators.note: to capture means to hold prisoner, so the reversed demon word surrounds the other piece
about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a devil is a demon

indicators.note: love in tennis is zero, so the round letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A lively fiend is about to seize someone lacking affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DEVIL into LIVED, which captures NE ('loveless one': ONE without O for love, zero in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: To have livened something is to have made it more lively or energetic.

clue.text: A yacht was wrecked — no hint of hope for me?

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the yacht smashed up, so its letters are rearranged
no means do without, so the picked letter is left out of the mix
a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked sailor, stranded with little hope, speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges A YACHT WAS less H, the first letter of 'hope' that 'no' removes. The definition is the speaker: the whole clue is the stranded one's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The marooned speaker is the person left alone after the shipwreck, a shipwrecked survivor.

clue.text: Officer looked up to by a learner but not journalist

indicators.note: but not means taking away, so the journalist letters are removed

parts.note: to be admired is to be looked up to
ED, short for editor, is a stock journalist
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: An officer respected by a trainee, but not by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link; ADMIRED loses ED to leave ADMIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior naval officer commanding a fleet.

clue.text: Petition stars outside entrance to show

indicators.note: outside means the stars word goes around the letter

parts.note: Orion is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A plea from celebrities waiting outside a theatre door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities but is the constellation Orion.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old word for a prayer, a petition to God.

clue.text: A sweetheart's getting caught in hiding places perhaps

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the caught letter goes into the sweetheart word

parts.note: a love is a sweetheart, and 'sweetheart's' gives loves (love is)
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lover's being caught in secret hideouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart's' is read as 'sweetheart is', giving LOVES; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoves are recesses in a wall, which could serve as nooks to hide in.

clue.text: Dog having white heifer as companion? That's an unusual thing

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
in Greek myth Io was turned into a white heifer by Zeus

explanation.surface: A mutt paired with a pale cow makes an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Io was a mortal lover of Zeus, changed into a white heifer to hide her from Hera.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object collected for its curiosity.

clue.text: I may be found out by this lab equipment!

definitions.text: I may be found out by this lab equipment!

parts.words: I may be found out by this lab equipment!
parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current, which a lab meter measures, not the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone fears being exposed by laboratory apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not the speaker but the symbol for electric current; 'found out' means measured.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is the instrument that measures current in amperes.

clue.text: Embarrass a bishop with a demand to keep quiet

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Shaming a bishop by telling him to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: A son's nurture say may be disturbed by these big beasts

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's upbringing could be upset by huge animals, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son's' supplies SONS; the apostrophe is ignored. 'may be disturbed' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These were huge carnivorous dinosaurs, the best known prehistoric monsters.

clue.text: Within country's borders it's somehow vulgar and gloomy

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so the vulgar word sits between the border letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: loud can mean vulgar or garish, as in a loud shirt

explanation.surface: Something brash and depressing inside the nation's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' gives the first and last letters of 'country's', C and Y, which go round LOUD; the words between the wordplay and 'gloomy' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast weather is dull and dark, so gloomy fits a grey sky.

clue.text: Pupils maybe hinder class — terrible fool must go!

indicators.note: terrible suggests something in a mess, so these letters are rearranged
must go means taken away, so the fool word is removed

parts.note: taken as written before the cut
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Students might disrupt a lesson, and an idiot must be expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: CLASS loses ASS ('fool must go') to leave CL; 'terrible' rearranges CL with HINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: School pupils are an example of youngsters, so 'maybe' marks this as an instance.
